tagline: Smart calendar scheduling for habits, tasks, breaks, and meetings.
verdictSummary: An auto-blocker for one calendar — read free/busy time, place recurring holds for habits and tasks inside preferred windows, move them when a real meeting lands on top — is a real weekend build. What doesn't come with it is two-way sync across multiple calendars, team coordination, and years of edge-case handling behind 'it never makes an embarrassing mistake.'
coreLoopDIY: A scheduled script that reads your calendar's free/busy time and places clearly marked holds for recurring habits and tasks inside their preferred windows, moving only the holds it created when a real meeting conflicts.
whyPeopleStillPay: Calendar automation is only valuable if it never makes an embarrassing mistake — people pay for that trustworthiness, which is mostly built from handling edge cases correctly, not from the core scheduling idea.
notes: A clear case where the product is really integrations plus trust, not the scheduling algorithm itself.
prompt:
Build a personal calendar auto-blocker for one calendar: define habits and tasks in a config file with a name, duration, an ideal time window, a target frequency per week, and a priority. On a schedule, read your calendar's free/busy time for the next week and place holds for unscheduled habits inside their windows, highest priority first. Tag every event the script creates with a distinct marker so it only ever moves or deletes events it made itself — never anything else on the calendar. If a real meeting lands on a hold, move that hold to the next free slot in its window and log the change. Provide a dry-run mode that prints next week's placements as a table before writing anything, and a clear-all command that removes every machine-created hold.

Do not build scheduling links, team coordination, or juggling multiple calendars at once — this manages one person's one calendar, and it should never touch or decline an event it didn't create itself.

faq.q: Can I import my existing Reclaim.ai habits and tasks?
faq.a: Not automatically — Reclaim's habit and task definitions live in its own system with no structured export. Recreating them in a config file is quick, since it's usually a short list.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: The holds it creates show up as normal events on any calendar app, including on your phone. Configuring new habits or tasks means editing a file, which isn't a phone-friendly workflow.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Hosting for the scheduled script, typically a few dollars a month — the calendar API itself is free at personal usage volumes.

faq.q: What's the one thing that doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: Trustworthy edge-case handling. Reclaim has been tuned against years of real calendar chaos — overlapping holds, last-minute cancellations, timezone changes; a personal script here handles the common cases and will occasionally need a manual nudge on the unusual ones.
